item.title: Paraguay's president impeached and under house arrest after bank collapse
item.description:
Santiago Peña was detained minutes after he was impeached by Congress, as protesters took to the streets demanding answers after the suspension of the Ueno bank Paraguay’s rightwing president has been placed under house arrest minutes after he was impeached by Congress, amid a severe crisis that left more than half the country’s population unable to access their bank accounts. Santiago Peña is being investigated about allegations he used his political influence to favour a bank that expanded exponentially under his government and was suspended this week after irregularities . item.title: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay at start of South America tour
item.description:
A mototaxi drives past a banner of Pope Leo XIV in Chiclayo, Peru, on Nov. 5, 2026, ahead of his trip to Latin America. AP Photo/Martin Mejia Pope Leo XIV travels to Latin America on Nov. 6, 2026, with a packed itinerary that will bring him through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It is Leo’s first trip to the region since his elevation to the papacy – and a homecoming for a pope who spent two decades in Peru and holds Peruvian citizenship. As a historian of Catholicism in the late 20th century , I couldn’t help but notice that the pope’s plans walk a fine line during a fraught political moment in Latin America. Leo plans to meet with the right-wing presidents of Argentina and Peru . He will also visit sites often associated with the progressive wing of the Catholic Church, including Casavalle, one of the poorest neighborhoods in Uruguay’s capital. Protesters from Geef Tegengas, a Dutch direct action group, clashed with police while breaking into a construction site at Westpoort, Amsterdam, where some members climbed a crane, lit flares and tied helium balloons to equipment. item.title: Cornell faculty declares 'no confidence' in university leadership
item.description:
Faculty senate passed resolution expressing deep discontent with school’s response to alleged fraternity rape Cornell University’s faculty senate approved a resolution on Friday declaring “no confidence” in the school’s top leaders, a symbolic gesture reflecting deep discontent on campus in the wake of a former student’s lawsuit saying she was gang-raped at a fraternity party in 2024. The resolution passed 75-50, with five faculty senators abstaining and five others not voting, according to an email sent to members of the faculty senate on Friday afternoon. Continue reading...

item.title: Qatari PM says US willing to seek solution to war with Iran
item.description:
President Trump said after meeting with his national security advisers Thursday that he'll soon decide whether to resume all-out war in Iran now that the midterms are over. Why it matters: The election was seen as an inflection point for Trump on whether to unleash a new wave of bombing to try to bring the war to an end. The president, at least for now, is considering three options: launch new strikes, continue to strangle Iran's regime economically, or cut a deal that includes significant concessions to the Iranians. On Thursday, Trump and his top national security advisers met on Iran for the first time since the election, as part of his weekly intelligence briefing, two U.S. officials said. item.title: Georgia Gov.-elect Bottoms reflects on historic victory and the path forward for Democrats
item.description:
Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms hugs her daughter Lincoln during an election night watch party in Atlanta, Ga., on Nov. 3, 2026. Megan Varner/Getty Images There are elections that change the political map. And then there are elections that make you wonder whether the land itself remembers. Georgia remembers. The auction blocks . The cotton fields . The lynching trees . The Black women who cleaned governors’ homes but could not dream of becoming governor themselves. And now Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected Georgia’s first Black woman governor . The first Black woman elected governor of any American state. Bottoms has traced her ancestry back five generations to an enslaved person on a plantation near Crawfordville, Georgia. An ancestor held in bondage on Georgia soil. item.title: Anthony Constantino’s Post-Election Crashout
item.description:
At an election eve rally in upstate New York, Republican congressional candidate Anthony Constantino told the crowd he had a dramatic announcement: Donald Trump was wrong about one thing. An audible gasp rippled through the converted airplane hangar. What could it possibly be? “Fake news” wasn’t accurate, Constantino said. “It’s actually evil news.” The candidate went on to gesture at the press pen and tell the crowd to take photos of its nefarious inhabitants. The campaign had not granted me credentials, so, like everyone else, I turned my attention to the people Constantino said “should be ashamed” of themselves. What Constantino did not seem to realize was that the most embarrassing thing about the event was that it was happening at all. item.title: Mayor-elect Nithya Raman inherits a Los Angeles full of promise and burdened by challenges
item.description:
Los Angeles, once California’s most reliably Republican stronghold, now faces a future under the leadership of a democratic socialist. Incumbent Mayor Karen Bass has lost her reelection bid to a friend-turned-rival, Councilmember and Mayor-elect Nithya Raman. Her election ushers in a new era for California’s largest city, decisively breaking it from the history that preceded it. Raman’s victory was unusual in some respects — she rode a national blue wave that toppled Republicans from Maine to California and, along the way, ousted the liberal, Black woman serving as mayor of Los Angeles — but natural, even overdue, in others. Raman, a 45-year-old Indian immigrant and mother of twins, was carried into office by younger voters and newer arrivals to L.A., those least burdened by the expectations or limitations of the city’s past .
